issues.issue: The clause makes this Confirmation prevail over the June 15, 2005 Master Repurchase Agreement on "any inconsistency", which is the hinge for whether the Confirmation's Termination Value and Buyer's Margin Amount terms displace Paragraph 4's margin machinery. A court must decide whether those terms are a permitted "modification" or an "inconsistency" overriding the Agreement.

The sentence says the Termination Value "will reflect changes in the market value of the parties' respective positions (including any embedded derivatives) and may be volatile", without tying "market value" to the Agreement's defined Market Value. The measure it announces is left undefined.

This disclosure describes Termination Value as a running market-value figure, while the operative "Termination Value" definition measures it only on an early termination resulting from an Event of Default. The two descriptions of the same term differ.
"Private Label MBS (AAA)" describes the Purchased Securities only by asset class and rating, with no issuer, tranche or amount stated in the line itself. Its scope depends entirely on the CUSIP line.

The roll date is "the 14th day of the next succeeding month following the Subsequent Transaction", which does not say whether the month runs from the preceding Repurchase Date or from the new Transaction's own Purchase Date. The reference point for "next succeeding month" is left unstated.
The fixed leg is expressed as a rate "p.a., fixed, adjusted", and nothing says what "adjusted" means or by reference to what. The word changes the rate actually payable.

"Notwithstanding the foregoing" has no identified antecedent in the Confirmation, leaving unclear which of the preceding terms the Buyer's termination right overrides. The rest of the mechanic is specific.

The Initial Transaction is defined by reference to "the first Repurchase Date specified below", but the Repurchase Date item appears above this entry in the Confirmation. The cross-reference points the wrong way.

Replacement securities need only be "acceptable to Buyer, in Buyer's discretion", and no time limit is fixed for Seller's substitution obligation. Both the standard of acceptability and the deadline are left open.

This clause obliges Seller to substitute whenever a Downgrade Event occurs, while the "Substitutions; Eligible Securities for Substitution" clause caps substitutions at twice a month and subjects further ones to Buyer's absolute discretion. The two cannot both operate without construction.

"Termination Value" turns on what a hypothetical "Dealer of recognized standing" "would be willing to pay" and on what is "necessary to compensate the non-defaulting party fairly", all as determined "in good faith". Each standard is open-textured and controls the size of the number.

The definition measures Termination Value only for an early termination "as a result of the occurrence of an Event of Default", yet the "Buyer's Margin Amount" clause requires a Positive or Negative Termination Value "as of any date" with no default. Reconciling the two requires construction.

Termination Value is payable "in addition to any other amounts owing ... pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 11 of the Agreement", raising whether the same loss is compensated twice. That must be read against the Termination Value definition's carve-out for Paragraph 11 amounts.

"As determined as if Buyer were the non-defaulting party" requires a valuation on a counterfactual assumption without saying what other facts are assumed. The content of the margin add-on is therefore unfixed.

This clause requires a Termination Value "as of any date", but the "Termination Value" definition supplies a figure only for early termination resulting from an Event of Default. A court must decide what the definition yields on an ordinary margin day.

The clause supplements Paragraph 4 of the Agreement by splitting Margin Deficits and Excesses into two independently calculated groups of Transactions. Whether calls and excesses may be aggregated across those groups, as Paragraph 4 would otherwise contemplate, is left to be construed.

The clause appoints Barclays itself to determine the Termination Value used in its own margin calls without stating any standard in the clause. What constrains that self-interested determination must be found elsewhere.

The "Termination Value" definition frames the figure as compensation of "the non-defaulting party", while this clause makes Barclays the Calculation Agent for margin purposes when neither party has defaulted. The two must be read together to know what is being measured.

The clause opens by making substitution subject to "Buyer's sole and absolute discretion" but then imposes objective conditions (equal or better quality, similar characteristics, equal Market Value) and allows two substitutions per month. Whether Seller has a qualified right to substitute twice monthly or needs Buyer's unfettered consent each time is genuinely uncertain.

The "Credit Rating" clause obliges Seller to substitute on every Downgrade Event, while this clause caps substitutions at twice a month and makes further ones discretionary for Buyer. The two provisions pull against each other.

The paragraph asks the Counterparty to sign and return within three Business Days, then provides that "Your failure to respond within such period shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the Transactions as against you". Whether and on what terms an unsigned Confirmation binds is left open by the same sentence that requests signature.

This clause requires substitution on every Downgrade Event, while the "Substitutions; Eligible Securities for Substitution" clause caps substitutions at twice a month and subjects further ones to Buyer's absolute discretion. The two cannot both operate as written.

"Termination Value" turns on what a hypothetical "Dealer of recognized standing" "would be willing to pay" and on what is "necessary to compensate the non-defaulting party fairly", all determined "in good faith". Each standard is open-textured and controls the amount.

The definition measures Termination Value only for early termination "as a result of the occurrence of an Event of Default", yet the "Buyer's Margin Amount" clause requires a Termination Value "as of any date" with no default. The two must be reconciled by construction.

Termination Value is payable "in addition to any other amounts owing ... pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 11 of the Agreement", which raises double-recovery. It must be read against the Termination Value definition's carve-out of Paragraph 11 amounts.
"As determined as if Buyer were the non-defaulting party" requires valuation on a counterfactual without saying what else is assumed. The content of the margin add-on is left unfixed.

The clause requires a Termination Value "as of any date", but the "Termination Value" definition supplies a figure only on early termination for an Event of Default. What the definition yields on an ordinary margin day must be construed.

The clause supplements Paragraph 4 of the Agreement by splitting Margin Deficits and Excesses into two independently calculated groups of Transactions. Whether margin may be aggregated across those groups, as Paragraph 4 would otherwise contemplate, is left to construction.

The clause appoints Barclays to determine the Termination Value used in its own margin calls without stating any standard in the clause itself. What constrains that self-interested determination must come from elsewhere.

The "Termination Value" definition frames the figure as compensation of "the non-defaulting party", while this clause makes Barclays Calculation Agent for margin purposes when neither party has defaulted. The provisions must be read together to know what is measured.

The clause opens by making substitution subject to "Buyer's sole and absolute discretion" yet then imposes objective conditions (equal or better quality, similar characteristics, equal Market Value) and allows two substitutions per month. Whether Seller has a qualified right to substitute twice monthly or needs Buyer's consent each time is genuinely uncertain.

The "Credit Rating" clause obliges Seller to substitute on every Downgrade Event, while this clause caps substitutions at twice monthly and makes further ones discretionary. The two pull against each other.

The paragraph requests signature and return within three Business Days, then provides that failure to respond "shall not affect the validity or enforceability of the Transactions as against you". Whether an unsigned Confirmation binds, and on whose terms, is left open by the same sentence.
